sub_units.name: Reading Comprehension
sub_units.content: Reading Comprehension tests the ability to understand, interpret, and analyze written passages. This topic covers identifying main ideas, drawing inferences, understanding tone and purpose, vocabulary in context, and answering detail-based and critical thinking questions. Strong reading comprehension skills are essential for all competitive exams and professional communication.

sub_units.name: Sentence Correction
sub_units.content: Sentence Correction involves identifying and fixing grammatical errors in sentences. This topic covers subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, pronoun usage, modifier placement, parallelism, and idiomatic expressions. Mastering sentence correction improves both written communication and performance in verbal ability sections of aptitude exams.

sub_units.name: Para Jumbles
sub_units.content: Para Jumbles require rearranging jumbled sentences into a coherent and logically ordered paragraph. This topic covers identifying opening and closing sentences, using transition words and connectors, maintaining thematic flow, and recognizing pronoun references. It tests logical sequencing skills and the ability to understand how ideas connect.

sub_units.name: Fill in the Blanks
sub_units.content: Fill in the Blanks problems test vocabulary, grammar, and contextual understanding by requiring the selection of appropriate words to complete sentences. This topic covers single blanks, double blanks, and cloze passages. It evaluates the ability to understand sentence meaning, identify word relationships, and apply correct usage in context.

sub_units.name: Synonyms & Antonyms
sub_units.content: Synonyms and Antonyms test vocabulary strength by requiring identification of words with similar or opposite meanings. This topic covers direct synonym and antonym pairs, contextual usage, and word analogy patterns. Building a strong vocabulary through synonyms and antonyms is fundamental for excelling in all verbal ability and reading comprehension tasks.

sub_units.name: Error Detection
sub_units.content: Error Detection involves identifying grammatical, syntactical, or logical errors within sentences or passages. This topic covers errors in articles, prepositions, conjunctions, verb forms, word order, and redundancy. It sharpens attention to detail and reinforces a thorough understanding of English grammar rules.

sub_units.name: Vocabulary Usage
sub_units.content: Vocabulary Usage tests the ability to use words correctly and effectively in different contexts. This topic covers commonly confused words, one-word substitutions, idioms and phrases, foreign words used in English, and word formation. A rich and precise vocabulary enhances both verbal reasoning performance and overall communication skills.

sub_units.name: Active & Passive Voice
sub_units.content: Active and Passive Voice involves understanding and converting sentences between active and passive constructions. This topic covers voice transformation rules for different tenses, modals, imperatives, and complex sentences. Mastering voice conversion is important for sentence correction, error detection, and effective writing.

sub_units.name: Direct & Indirect Speech
sub_units.content: Direct and Indirect Speech (also called reported speech) involves converting quoted speech into reported form and vice versa. This topic covers changes in tense, pronouns, time expressions, and sentence structure during conversion. It is a key grammar concept tested in verbal ability sections and essential for accurate communication.

sub_units.name: Critical Reading
sub_units.content: Critical Reading goes beyond basic comprehension to evaluate the logic, validity, and strength of arguments presented in a text. This topic covers identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, recognizing bias, distinguishing fact from opinion, and assessing the author's reasoning. It develops advanced analytical skills needed for higher-level verbal reasoning tasks.
